<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P>NOTE A &#150; SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES (continued)</P>
<P><U>Revenue and Cost Recognition (continued)</U></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">Job costs include all direct materials, and labor
costs and those indirect costs related to production of approved medical
devices. Selling, general and administrative costs are charged to expense as
incurred.</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><U>Cost of Goods Sold</U></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">Job costs include all direct materials, and labor
costs and those indirect costs related to production. Selling, general and
administrative costs are charged to expense as incurred. </P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><U>Advertising</U></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">Expenses related to specific jobs are allocated
and classified as costs of goods sold. Expenses not related to specific jobs are
recorded as general and administrative expenses. Advertising expense for the
years ended December 31, 2007 and 2006 totaled $279, and $3,067,
respectively.</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><U>Principles of Consolidation</U></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">These consolidated financial statements are
presented based on the generally accepted accounting principle of consolidation
and merger. An acquisition of a company occurs when one enterprise pays cash, or
issues stock or debt for all or part of the voting stock of another enterprise.
The acquired enterprise remains intact as a separate legal entity. The
parent-subsidiary relationship is accounted for as a purchase, and it is
referred to as an acquisition. Consolidated statements present the results of
operations and the financial position of a parent company and its subsidiaries
essentially as if the group were a single enterprise with one or more branches
or divisions.</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">The consolidated financial statements include the
accounts of Meditecnic, Inc. and Meditecnic, S.A. Intercompany balances have
been eliminated in these consolidated statements.</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><U>Stock</U></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">The Company has authorized common stock and has
also authorized preferred stock see Note H.</P>

<P><U></U></P>
<P><U>Recently Issued Accounting Pronouncements</U></P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in">In June 2008, the FASB ratified EITF Issue No.
08-3, &#147;Accounting for Lessees for Maintenance Deposits Under Lease Arrangements&#148;
(EITF 08-3). EITF 08-3 provides guidance for accounting for nonrefundable
maintenance deposits. It also provides revenue recognition accounting guidance
for the lessor. EITF 08-3 is effective for fiscal years beginning after December
15, 2008. The Company does not expect the&nbsp; impact of EITF 08-3 on its
consolidated financial position and results of operations to be material.
&nbsp;</P>
<P>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In May
2008, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#147;FASB&#148;) issued SFAS No. 162,
&#147;The Hierarchy of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles.&#148; This statement
identifies the sources of accounting principles and the framework for selecting
the principles to be used in the preparation of financial statements presented
in conformity&nbsp;with generally accepted accounting principles in the United
States. This statement is effective 60 days following the approval of the
Securities and Exchange Commission. The Company does not expect the effects of
adopting this statement to be significant.</P>
<P></P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in">In April 2008, the FASB issued FSP 142-3,
&#147;Determination of the Useful Life of Intangible Assets&#148;, (FSP 142-3). FSP 142-3
amends the factors that should be considered in developing renewal or extension
assumptions used to determine the useful life of a recognized intangible asset
under SFAS No. 142, &#147;Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets&#148;. FSP 142-3 is
effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2008. The Company does
not expect the adoption of FSP 142-3 will have a material impact on the
Company&#146;s consolidated financial position, results of operations and cash
flows.</P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in">In March 2008, the FASB issued SFAS No. 161
&#147;Disclosures about Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities amendment of
FASB Statement No. 133&#148; (&#147;SFAS 161&#148;).&nbsp;&nbsp;This statement changes the
disclosure requirements for derivative instruments and hedging
activities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Entities are required to provide enhanced disclosures
stating how and why an entity uses derivative instruments; how derivatives and
related hedged items are accounted for under SFAS No. 133, &#147;Accounting for
Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities&#148; (&#147;SFAS 133&#148;) and its related
interpretations; and how derivative instruments and related hedge items affect
an entity&#146;s financial position, financial performance and cash
flows.&nbsp;&nbsp;SFAS 161 is effective in fiscal years beginning after November
15. 2008 and is required to be adopted by the Company in the first quarter of
fiscal year 2010.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company does not expect the adoption of SFAS
161 will have a material impact on the Company&#146;s disclosures.</P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in">&nbsp;In December 2007, FASB issued SFAS No. 160
&#147;Non-controlling Interest in Consolidated Financial Statements&#148;. SFAS No. 160
amends Accounting Research Bulletin No.51, Consolidated Financial Statements, to
establish accounting and reporting standards for the non-controlling interest in
a subsidiary and for the deconsolidation of a subsidiary.&nbsp;&nbsp;SFAS No.
160 defines &#147;a non-controlling interest, sometimes called a minority interest,
is the portion of equity in a subsidiary not attributable, directly or
indirectly, to a parent&#148;.&nbsp;&nbsp;The objective of SFAS No. 160 is to improve
the relevance, comparability, and transparency of the financial information that
a reporting entity provides in its consolidated financial
statements.&nbsp;&nbsp;SFAS No. 160 is effective for fiscal years, and interim
periods within those fiscal years, beginning on or after December 15, 2008 and
is required to be adopted by the Company in the first quarter of fiscal year
2010.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is evaluating the impact, if any, of the adoption
of SFAS No. 160.&nbsp;&nbsp;It is not expected to have material impact on the
Company&#146;s financial position, results of operations and cash flows.</P>
<P>In March 2008, the FASB issued SFAS No. 161 &#147;Disclosures about Derivative
Instruments and Hedging Activities amendment of FASB Statement No. 133&#148; (&#147;SFAS
161&#148;).&nbsp;&nbsp;This statement changes the disclosure requirements for
derivative instruments and hedging activities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Entities are required
to provide enhanced disclosures stating how and why an entity uses derivative
instruments; how derivatives and related hedged items are accounted for under
SFAS No. 133, &#147;Accounting for Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities&#148;
(&#147;SFAS 133&#148;) and its related interpretations; and how derivative instruments and
related hedge items affect an entity&#146;s financial position, financial performance
and cash flows.&nbsp;&nbsp;SFAS 161 is effective in fiscal years beginning after
November 15. 2008 and is required to be adopted by the Company in the first
quarter of fiscal year 2010.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company does not expect the adoption
of SFAS 161 will have a material impact on the Company&#146;s disclosures.</P>
<P>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In December 2007, the FASB issued SFAS No. 141
(revised 2007), &#147;Business Combinations.&#148; SFAS No. 141R changes the accounting
for business combinations in a number of areas including the treatment of
contingent consideration, preacquisition contingencies, transaction costs,
in-process research and development and restructuring </P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">Recently Issued Accounting Pronouncements
(continued)costs. In addition, under SFAS No. 141R, changes in an acquired
entity&#146;s deferred tax assets and uncertain tax positions after the measurement
period will impact income tax expense. This statement will be effective as of
the beginning of an entity&#146;s first fiscal year that begins after December 15,
2008. This statement, when adopted, will change the Company&#146;s accounting
treatment for business combinations on a prospective basis.</P>
<P>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In February 2007, the FASB issued SFAS No. 159,
&#147;The Fair Value Option for Financial Assets and Financial Liabilities.&#148; This
statement permits entities to choose to measure many financial instruments and
certain other items at fair value. The objective is to improve financial
reporting by providing entities with the opportunity to mitigate volatility in
reported earnings caused by measuring related assets and liabilities differently
without having to apply complex hedge accounting provisions. This statement is
expected to expand the use of fair value measurement. SFAS No. 159 is effective
as of the beginning of an entity&#146;s first fiscal year that begins after November
15, 2007. The Company adopted adopt SFAS No. 159 during the first quarter of
fiscal 2008.</P>
<P>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In September 2006, the FASB issued SFAS No.
157, &#147;Fair Value Measurements&#148;. This statement defines fair value, establishes a
framework for measuring fair value in generally accepted accounting principles,
and expands disclosures about fair value measurements. SFAS No. 157 is effective
for financial statements issued for fiscal years beginning after November 15,
2007, and interim periods within those fiscal years. The Company is currently in
the process of determining the effects of adopting this statement in its
consolidated financial statements. In November 2007, the FASB approved the
deferral of the effective date of SFAS No. 157 for one year for all nonfinancial
assets and nonfinancial liabilities, except for those items that are recognized
or disclosed at fair value in the financial statements on a recurring basis.
</P>

Annual taxes and patent license</FONT></PRE><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> fees and legal costs associated therewith are expensed as incurred.&nbsp; The continuing carrying value of</FONT></PRE><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> patents is assessed based upon the Company's operating experience, expected cash flows from related</FONT></PRE><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">products and other factors as deemed appropriate.&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV>&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV>NOTE I - INCOME TAXES</DIV>
<DIV><PRE><FONT face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">The Company follows Statement of Financial Accounting Standards ("SFAS") No. 109,&nbsp; "Accounting for Income</FONT></PRE><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> Taxes", which requires the recognition of deferred tax liabilities and assets for the expected</FONT></PRE><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> future tax consequences of events that have been included in the financial statements or tax returns.</FONT></PRE><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> Under this method, deferred income taxes are recognized for the tax consequences in future years of</FONT></PRE><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> differences between the tax bases of assets and liabilities and their financial reporting </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">amounts are each year-end based on enacted tax laws and statutory tax rates applicable to the periods in</FONT></PRE><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> which the differences are expected to affect taxable income.&nbsp; </FONT></PRE><PRE><FONT face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</PRE>Valuation allowances are
established, when necessary, to reduce deferred tax assets to the amount
expected to be realized.</DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> The provision for income taxes represents the tax payable for the period and the change during the period </FONT></PRE><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">in deferred tax assets and liabilities.&nbsp; As of December 31, 2007 and 2006 there were no deferred tax </FONT></PRE><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">liabilities or assets. As of December 31, 2007, the Company had net operating loss carryforwards for </FONT></PRE><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">federal purposes of over $150,000. The federal net operating loss carryforward have begun expiring.</FONT></PRE><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> The utilization of net operating loss carryforwards may be limited under the provisions of Internal </FONT></PRE><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">Revenue Code Section 382 and similar state provisions.</FONT></PRE></DIV>

<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">Foreign currency transaction gains and losses result from a change in exchange rates between the functional </FONT></PRE><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">currency of the Company and the currency in which a foreign transaction is denominated.&nbsp; These gains or</FONT></PRE><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> losses are comprised of actual currency gains or losses realized upon settlement or foreign currency </FONT></PRE><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">transactions and expected (unrealized) currency gains or losses on unsettled foreign currency transactions.</FONT></PRE></DIV>

<P>&nbsp;</P>
<P>NOTE R &#150; GOING CONCERN</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">Under the going concern assumption, an entity is
ordinarily viewed as continuing in business for the foreseeable </P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">future with neither the intention nor the
necessity of liquidation, ceasing trading, or seeking protection from
creditors</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;pursuant to laws or regulations.
Accordingly, assets and liabilities are recorded on the basis that the entity
will be </P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">able to realize its assets and discharge its
liabilities in the normal course of business.</P>
<P>&nbsp;</P>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">The Company has had limited operations to date other than the acquisition of the patents and license rights.</FONT></PRE><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">&nbsp; In March 1998 the Company raised $100,000 in an offering of common stock.&nbsp; In 2000 the Company sold </FONT></PRE><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">$3,000,000 in Common Stock.&nbsp; The Company is in the research and development stage of its products.&nbsp; </FONT></PRE><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">Research and development costs were $223,598 in fiscal 2001, $230,817 in fiscal 2000 and $206,508 in</FONT></PRE><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> fiscal 1999.&nbsp; </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE><FONT face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">Research and development was carried out by a (previous to the acquisition) non-affiliated entity, Meditecnic SA,</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> on a contract basis. The Company exercised its option to purchase all of the capital stock of Meditecnic SA for </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">CHF 400,000 granted November 5, 2002, of which CHF 300,000&nbsp; ($195,720) was paid in November 2001 and</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> is accounted for on the December 31, 2001 balance sheet as a deposit.&nbsp; </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">The Company has also loaned funds to Meditecnic SA prior to the exercising of the purchase agreement. In addition </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">the Company placed a CHF 60,000 deposit for the purchase of patents in December 2000&nbsp; ($38,346) and a </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">CHF 100,000 ($60.390) for the purchase of an additional patent in February 2001.Due to the exercising of the</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> subsidiary stock purchase the intercompany balances have been eliminated.&nbsp; </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">The Company had cash on hand and marketable
securities of $120,714 at December 31, 2007, which is not </P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">believed to be sufficient to fund the Company's
operations until at the end of fiscal 2008.</P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">NOTE T &#150; ACQUISITION </P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">An acquisition of a company occurs when one
enterprise pays cash, or issues stock or debt for all or part of the voting
stock of another enterprise. The acquired enterprise remains intact as a
separate legal entity. The parent-subsidiary relationship is accounted for as a
purchase, and it is referred to as an acquisition. </P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">Meditecnic, S.A. originally authorized and issued
One Hundred (100) bearer shares of stock, which were issued to one (1)
shareholder. These stocks were cancelled as part of the acquisition agreement.
In an acquisition the stock disclosures are presented by retroactively stating
the equity accounts as of the earliest period presented to give effect to the
new capital structure subsequent to the acquisition. </P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify">No additional shares of
stock will be issued as part of this purchase option agreement. Therefore the
equity section of the financial statements presented reports the total number of
shares issued as of December 31, 2006 as Seven Million Five Hundred Twenty Seven
Thousand Four Hundred Eighty Five (7,527,485) shares of common stock. </P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify">Meditecnic, SA had assets
valued at $420,017; therefore the Seven Million Five Hundred Twenty Seven
Thousand Four Hundred Eighty Five (7,527,485) share of common stock on shares of
Meditecnic, SA Corp still issued and outstanding had a value of .0558 cents per
share at the date of acquisition. Meditecnic, Inc. had assets on the books
valuing Two Million Six Hundred Twenty Thousand Four Hundred Sixty Three
(2,620,463) resulting in a stock value of .348 cents per share prior to the
acquisition. </P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify">The acquisition resulted in
an increase in the value of the outstanding Seven Million Five Hundred Twenty
Seven Thousand Four Hundred Eighty Five (7,527,485) shares of common stock to
.404 cents per share. This resulted in a reverse dilution of .056 cents per
share equal to a .161 percent dilution.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify">Per the purchase option
agreement all One Hundred (100) shares of stock were obtained from Meditecnic,
S.A. when the option was exercised on June 6, 2002. The Company stock was
purchased at fair market value. Therefore, these financial statements are
presented as if the acquisition had occurred during the periods presented.</P>
<DIV>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;

<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">A summary of significant accounting policies of Meditecnic, Inc. (Predecessor, Viking Broadcasting Corporation) is presented to assist in </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">understanding the Company&#146;s financial statements. The financial statements and notes are representations of the Company&#146;s management </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">who are responsible for their integrity and objectivity. These accounting policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles and </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">have been consistently applied in the preparation of the accompanying financial statements. </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">The accompanying financial statements are unaudited, but in the opinion of the management of the Company, contain all adjustments, </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">consisting of only normal recurring accruals, necessary to present fairly the financial position at September 30, 2005, the results of operations </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2008 and 2007, and the cash flows for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2008 </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">and 2007.</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">Reference is made to the Company's Form 10-Kfor the year ended December 31, 2007.&nbsp; The results of operations for the three and nine months </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">ended September 30, 2008 are not necessarily indicative of the results of operations to be expected for the full fiscal year ending December 31, </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">2008.</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><U></U>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><U>Organization, Nature of Business and Trade
Name</U></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><U></U>&nbsp;</P>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">Meditecnic, Inc. (The &#147;Company&#148;) was incorporated in the State of Nevada on March 24, 1998. Meditecnic, Inc. is the successor by merger </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">on April 18, 1998 with Viking Broadcasting Corporation, (&#147;Viking&#148;) a Utah corporation incorporated on May 1, 1984 as Carrigan Gold </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">Corporation. Viking was originally formed to sell and deal in minerals, oil and gas properties. This venture and an investment in broadcasting </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">properties were unsuccessful. Because of the unsuccessful ventures, prior to the merger and the subsequent acquisition of certain </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">patent rights, Viking was inactive and had discontinued operations.</FONT>&nbsp; </PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</PRE></DIV>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">The Company has acquired the technology related
to its endoscopic applications from Meditecnic, S.A. (&#147;Meditecnic&#148;), which
also</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;performs research and development for the
Company. </P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify">The financials include the
accounts of Meditecnic, Inc., Viking Broadcasting Corporation and Meditecnic,
S.A. a wholly owned subsidiary. On April 18, 1998, Meditecnic, Inc. merged with
Viking Broadcasting Corporation being the surviving company and establishing the
surviving entity&#146;s name to be Meditecnic, Inc. The Company's primary business is
developing and marketing advanced products for dental and endoscopic
applications.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">Prior to April 18, 1998, Meditecnic, Inc. had been a privately owned and operated development stage company. The Company has not </PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">generated any significant revenues from its operations and is defined as a development stage company per SFAS No. 7.</PRE></DIV>

and preventing and detecting fraud. The Company&#146;s system of internal accounting
control is </P>

related accumulated depreciation are removed from the accounts, and any
resulting gain or loss is reflected in income for the period. </P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P><U>Use of Estimates</U></P>
<P>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">The preparation of financial statements in
accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America
requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported
amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosure of contingent assets and
liabilities at the date of the financial statements and the reported amounts of
revenues and expenses during the reporting period.&nbsp; A change in
managements&#146; estimates or assumptions could have a material impact on
Meditecnic, Inc.&#146;s financial condition and results of operations during the
period in which such changes occurred. Actual results could differ from those
estimates. Meditecnic, Inc.&#146;s financial statements reflect all adjustments that
management believes are necessary for the fair presentation of their financial
condition and results of operations for the periods presented.</P>
<DIV><PRE>&nbsp;</PRE></DIV>
<DIV><U>Cash and Cash Equivalents</U></DIV>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">For purposes of the statement of cash flows, the
Company considers all short-term debt securities purchased with maturity of
three months or less to be cash equivalents. Cash equivalents are carried at
cost, which approximates market. The Company maintains cash in bank deposits
accounts, which, at times, may exceed federally insured limits or are in foreign
banks.</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P><U>Revenue and Cost Recognition</U></P>
<P><U></U></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">The Company reports income and expenses on the
accrual basis of accounting, whereby income is recorded when it is earned and
expenses recorded when they are incurred. In this specific industry revenue is
generated from the sale of approved devices. No devices have been approved to
this date; therefore, no revenue from operations has been generated. </P>

clear=all>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;

<P><U>Revenue and Cost Recognition (continued)</U></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">Job costs include all direct materials, and labor
costs and those indirect costs related to production of approved medical
devices. Selling, general and administrative costs are charged to expense as
incurred.</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><U></U>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><U>Cost of Goods Sold</U></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><U></U>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">Job costs include all direct materials, and labor
costs and those indirect costs related to production. Selling, general and
administrative costs are charged to expense as incurred. </P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><U>Advertising</U></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><U></U>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">Expenses related to specific jobs are allocated
and classified as costs of goods sold. Expenses not related to specific jobs are
recorded as general and administrative expenses.</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><U>Principles of Consolidation</U></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><U></U>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">These consolidated financial statements are
presented based on the generally accepted accounting principle of consolidation
and merger. These principles state that a new enterprise is formed through the
exchange of stock, or payment of cash or other property, or the issue of debt
instruments. Consolidated statements are then presented based on the combining
of the results of operations and the financial position of both companies
essentially as if the two were a single entity in the periods presented.</P>
<P><U></U>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">The consolidated financial statements include the
accounts of Meditecnic, Inc. and Meditecnic, S.A. Intercompany balances have
been eliminated in these consolidated statements.</P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><U>Recently Issued Accounting Pronouncements
(continued)</U></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">with generally accepted accounting principles in
the United States. This statement is effective 60 days following the approval of
the Securities and Exchange Commission. The Company does not expect the effects
of adopting this statement to be significant.</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; TEXT-ALIGN: justify">In April 2008, the FASB
issued FSP 142-3, &#147;Determination of the Useful Life of Intangible Assets&#148;, (FSP
142-3). FSP 142-3 amends the factors that should be considered in developing
renewal or extension assumptions used to determine the useful life of a
recognized intangible asset under SFAS No. 142, &#147;Goodwill and Other Intangible
Assets&#148;. FSP 142-3 is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15,
2008. The Company does not expect the adoption of FSP 142-3 will have a material
impact on the Company&#146;s consolidated financial position, results of operations
and cash flows.</P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; TEXT-ALIGN: justify">In March 2008, the FASB
issued SFAS No. 161 &#147;Disclosures about Derivative Instruments and Hedging
Activities amendment of FASB Statement No. 133&#148; (&#147;SFAS 161&#148;).&nbsp;&nbsp;This
statement changes the disclosure requirements for derivative instruments and
hedging activities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Entities are required to provide enhanced
disclosures stating how and why an entity uses derivative instruments; how
derivatives and related hedged items are accounted for under SFAS No. 133,
&#147;Accounting for Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities&#148; (&#147;SFAS 133&#148;) and
its related interpretations; and how derivative instruments and related hedge
items affect an entity&#146;s financial position, financial performance and cash
flows.&nbsp;&nbsp;SFAS 161 is effective in fiscal years beginning after November
15. 2008 and is required to be adopted by the Company in the first quarter of
fiscal year 2010.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company does not expect the adoption of SFAS
161 will have a material impact on the Company&#146;s disclosures.</P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;In December 2007, FASB
issued SFAS No. 160 &#147;Non-controlling Interest in Consolidated Financial
Statements&#148;. SFAS No. 160 amends Accounting Research Bulletin No.51,
Consolidated Financial Statements, to establish accounting and reporting
standards for the non-controlling interest in a subsidiary and for the
deconsolidation of a subsidiary.&nbsp;&nbsp;SFAS No. 160 defines &#147;a
non-controlling interest, sometimes called a minority interest, is the portion
of equity in a subsidiary not attributable, directly or indirectly, to a
parent&#148;.&nbsp;&nbsp;The objective of SFAS No. 160 is to improve the relevance,
comparability, and transparency of the financial information that a reporting
entity provides in its consolidated financial statements.&nbsp;&nbsp;SFAS No.
160 is effective for fiscal years, and interim periods within those fiscal
years, beginning on or after December 15, 2008 and is required to be adopted by
the Company in the first quarter of fiscal year 2010.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is
evaluating the impact, if any, of the adoption of SFAS No. 160.&nbsp;&nbsp;It is
not expected to have material impact on the Company&#146;s financial position,
results of operations and cash flows.</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">In March 2008, the FASB issued SFAS No. 161
&#147;Disclosures about Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities amendment of
FASB Statement No. 133&#148; (&#147;SFAS 161&#148;).&nbsp;&nbsp;This statement changes the
disclosure requirements for derivative instruments and hedging
activities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Entities are required to provide enhanced disclosures
stating how and why an entity uses derivative instruments; how derivatives and
related hedged items are accounted for under SFAS No. 133, &#147;Accounting for
Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities&#148; (&#147;SFAS 133&#148;) and its related
interpretations; and how derivative instruments and related hedge items affect
an entity&#146;s financial position, financial performance and cash
flows.&nbsp;&nbsp;SFAS 161 is effective in fiscal years beginning after November
15. 2008 and is required to be adopted by the Company in the first quarter of
fiscal year 2010.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company does not expect the adoption of SFAS
161 will have a material impact on the Company&#146;s disclosures.</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">In December 2007, the FASB issued SFAS No. 141
(revised 2007), &#147;Business Combinations.&#148; SFAS No. 141R changes the accounting
for business combinations in a number of areas including the treatment of
contingent consideration, preacquisition contingencies, transaction costs,
in-process research and development and restructuring costs. In addition, under
SFAS No. 141R, changes in an acquired entity&#146;s deferred tax assets and uncertain
tax positions after the measurement period will impact income tax expense. This
statement will be effective as of the beginning of an entity&#146;s first fiscal year
that begins after December 15, 2008. This statement, when adopted, will change
the Company&#146;s accounting treatment for business combinations on a prospective
basis.</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In February 2007,
the FASB issued SFAS No. 159, &#147;The Fair Value Option for Financial Assets and
Financial Liabilities.&#148; This statement permits entities to choose to measure
many financial instruments and certain other items at fair value. The objective
is to improve financial reporting by providing entities with the opportunity to
mitigate volatility in reported earnings caused by measuring related assets and
liabilities differently without having to apply complex hedge accounting
provisions. This statement is expected to expand the use of fair value
measurement. SFAS No. 159 is effective as of the beginning of an entity&#146;s first
fiscal year that begins after November 15, 2007. The Company adopted adopt SFAS
No. 159 during the first quarter of fiscal 2008.</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In September 2006,
the FASB issued SFAS No. 157, &#147;Fair Value Measurements&#148;. This statement defines
fair value, establishes a framework for measuring fair value in generally
accepted accounting principles, and expands disclosures about fair value
measurements. SFAS No. 157 is effective for financial statements issued for
fiscal years beginning after November 15, 2007, and interim periods within those
fiscal years. The Company is currently in the process of determining the effects
of adopting this statement in its consolidated financial statements. In November
2007, the FASB approved the deferral of the effective date of SFAS No. 157 for
one year for all nonfinancial assets and nonfinancial liabilities, except for
those items that are recognized or disclosed at fair value in the financial
statements on a recurring basis. </P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">NOTE B &#150; ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">Accounts receivable is defined as amounts due
from customers for goods and services provided in the normal course of business
operations.&nbsp; All amounts are based on actual costs incurred.</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">The receivables that total the amount on the
balance sheet are from invoices issued to long time customers that are
considered good credit risks and have a history of paying invoices within a
reasonable length of time.&nbsp; Therefore we have determined through analysis
of past historical experience for this Company the allowance for bad debt would
be less than one half of one percent (.5%) of the receivables listed on the
books.</P>

<DIV><PRE><FONT face="Times New Roman">NOTE I - INCOME TAXES</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE><FONT face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">The Company follows Statement of Financial Accounting Standards ("SFAS") No. 109, "Accounting for Income Taxes", which</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> requires the recognition of deferred tax liabilities and assets for the expected future tax consequences of events that have been </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">included in the financial statements or tax returns. Under this method, deferred income taxes are recognized for the tax </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">consequences in future years of differences between the tax bases of assets and liabilities and their financial reporting amounts </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">are each year-end based on enacted tax laws and statutory tax rates applicable to the periods in which the differences are</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> expected to affect taxable income.&nbsp; </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE><FONT face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">Valuation allowances are established, when necessary, to reduce deferred tax assets to the amount expected to be realized. The </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">provision for income taxes represents the tax payable for the period and the change during the period in deferred tax assets </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">and liabilities.&nbsp; As of September 30, 2006 and 2005 there were no deferred tax liabilities or assets. As of September 30, 2008,</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> the Company had net operating loss carryforwards for federal purposes of over $150,000. The federal net operating loss </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">carryforward have begun expiring. The utilization of net operating loss carryforwards may be limited under the provisions of</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> Internal Revenue Code Section 382 and similar state provisions.</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">The Company has no U.S. operations and is incorporated in Nevada, which levies no income tax on corporations.</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">Due to the inherent uncertainty in forecasts and future events and operating results, the Company has provided for a valuation</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> allowance in an amount equal to gross deferred tax assets resulting in no net deferred tax assets or liabilities for the periods </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">audited.</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">&nbsp; 46<HR></FONT></PRE></DIV>

<P>&nbsp;</P>
<P>NOTE R &#150; GOING CONCERN</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">Under the going concern assumption, an entity is
ordinarily viewed as continuing in business for the foreseeable future with
neither the intention nor the necessity of liquidation, ceasing trading, or
seeking protection from creditors pursuant to laws or regulations. Accordingly,
assets and liabilities are recorded on the basis that the entity will be able to
realize its assets and discharge its liabilities in the normal course of
business.</P>

48 </DIV>

<P>NOTE R &#150; GOING CONCERN (continued)</P>
<P>&nbsp;</P>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">The Company has had limited operations to date other than the acquisition of the patents and license rights.&nbsp; In March 1998 the</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> Company raised $100,000 in an offering of common stock.&nbsp; In 2000 the Company sold $3,000,000 in Common Stock.&nbsp; The </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">Company is in the research and development stage of its products. </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE><FONT face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">Research and development was carried out by a (previous to the acquisition) non-affiliated entity, Meditecnic SA, on a contract</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> basis. The Company exercised its option to purchase all of the capital stock of Meditecnic SA for CHF 400,000 granted </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">November 5, 2001, of which CHF 300,000 ($195,720) was paid in November 2001 and is accounted for on the December </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">31, 2001 balance sheet as a deposit.</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">The Company has also loaned funds to Meditecnic SA prior to the exercising of the purchase agreement. In addition the</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> Company placed a CHF 60,000 deposit for the purchase of patents in December 2000 ($38,346) and a CHF 100,000 ($60,390) </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">for the purchase of an additional patent in February 2001.&nbsp; Due to the exercising of the subsidiary stock purchase the</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> intercompany balances have been eliminated.</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">NOTE S - NET LOSS PER COMMON SHARE
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">Net loss per share is calculated in accordance
with SFAS No. 128, &#147;Earnings Per Share.&#148; The weighted &#150;average number </P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">of common shares outstanding during each period
is used to compute basic loss per share.</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">Basic net loss per common share is based on the
weighted-average number of share of common stock of Seven Million Five Hundred
Twenty Seven Thousand Four Hundred Eighty Five (7,527,485) outstanding.</P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: center" align=center><A name=_Aci_Pg15></A><B>MEDITECNIC,
INC., (A Development Stage Company)</B></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: center" align=center><B>(Predecessor, Viking Broadcasting
Corporation)</B></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: center" align=center><B>NOTES TO FINANCIAL
STATEMENTS</B></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">NOTE T &#150; ACQUISITION</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">An acquisition of a company occurs when one
enterprise pays cash, or issues stock or debt for all or part of the voting
stock of another enterprise. The acquired enterprise remains intact as a
separate legal entity. The parent-subsidiary relationship is accounted for as a
purchase, and it is referred to as an acquisition. </P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">Meditecnic, S.A. originally authorized and issued
One Hundred (100) bearer shares of stock, which were issued to one (1)
shareholder. These stocks were cancelled as part of the acquisition agreement.
In an acquisition the stock disclosures are presented by retroactively stating
the equity accounts as of the earliest period presented to give effect to the
new capital structure subsequent to the acquisition. </P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify">No additional shares of
stock will be issued as part of this purchase option agreement. Therefore the
equity section of the financial statements presented reports the total number of
shares issued as of December 31, 2005 as Seven Million Five Hundred Twenty Seven
Thousand Four Hundred Eighty Five (7,527,485) shares of common stock.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify">Meditecnic, SA had assets
valued at $420,017; therefore the Seven Million Five Hundred Twenty Seven
Thousand Four Hundred Eighty Five (7,527,485) share of common stock on shares of
Meditecnic, SA Corp still issued and outstanding had a value of .0558 cents per
share at the date of acquisition.&nbsp; Meditecnic, Inc. had assets on the books
valuing Two Million six Hundred Twenty Thousand Four Hundred Sixty Three
(2,620,463) resulting in a stock value of .348 cents per share prior to the
acquisition.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify">The acquisition resulted in
an increase in the value of the outstanding Seven Million Five Hundred Twenty
Seven Thousand Four Hundred Eighty Five (7,527,485) shares of common stock to
.404 cents per share.&nbsp; This resulted in a reverse dilution of .056 cents
per share equal to a .161 percent dilution.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify">Per the purchase option
agreement all One Hundred (100) shares of stock were obtained from Meditecnic,
S.A. when the option was exercised on June 6, 2002.&nbsp; The Company stock was
purchased at fair market value.&nbsp; Therefore, these financial statements are
presented as if the acquisition had occurred during the periods presented.</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN-LEFT: 1in; TEXT-INDENT: -1in; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><B>ITEM
14.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; CHANGES IN AND DISAGREEMENTS WITH
ACCOUNTANTS ON ACCOUNTING AND FINANCIAL DISCLOSURE.</B></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&nbsp;</P>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; On March 11, 2002 the Registrant's dismissed its former independent accountant Crouch, Bierwolf &amp; Associates</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> ("CBA").&nbsp; The report by CBA on the financial statements of the Registrant dated May 23, 2001, including balance sheets as </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">of December 31, 2000 and 1999 and the statements of operations, cash flows and statement of stockholders' equity for the </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">years ended December 31, 2000 and 1999 and the period inception (March 24, 1988) to December 31, 2000 did not contain </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">an adverse opinion or a disclaimer of opinion, or was qualified or modified as to uncertainty, audit scope or accounting </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">principles.&nbsp; During the period covered by the financial statements through the date of dismissal of the former accountant, </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">there were no disagreements with the former accountant on any matter of accounting principles or practices, financial </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">statement disclosure, or auditing scope or procedure.&nbsp; </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The Registrant reported in the above 8-K, as amended, that on March 11, 2002 the Registrant engaged </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">Tanner +Co., as its new independent accountants. In that Form 8-K, the Registrant stated &#147; Prior to the&nbsp; engagement </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">of Tanner + Co., the&nbsp; Registrant&nbsp; did not consult with Tanner + Co., on the&nbsp; application&nbsp; of accounting&nbsp; principles to any</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> specific transaction nor the type of audit opinion that&nbsp; might&nbsp; be&nbsp; rendered&nbsp; on the&nbsp; Registrant's&nbsp; financial&nbsp; statements.&nbsp; </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">CBA was provided by the disclosure set forth above but failed to respond&nbsp; to many requests over a period of months that</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> it provide the Registrant with a letter to the effect that it or did not agree with the above statements as far as they related to </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">CBA. The dismissal of CBA and the subsequent engagement of Tanner + Co. was approved by the board of directors.&#148;</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The engagement of Tanner+Co. did not lead to any substantive work being performed by them.</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; On December 27, 2007, the Registrant engaged The Blackwing Group. LLC as its independent auditor. </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">This engagement was approved by the Board of Directors. Due to the length of time since the financial statements were</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman"> not audited, and the fact that CBA was no longer in business, and could not supply The Blackwing Group LLC with </FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT face="Times New Roman">any information regarding the prior audits, the Registrant determined to cause its financial statements to be reaudited for</FONT></PRE></DIV>
<DIV><PRE style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'">fiscal 1999 and 2000, and the periodic reports amended for those periods. </FONT></PRE></DIV>
